title: Food Prices in Lagos Today: Rice, Garri, Beans, Yam & Eggs (2026)
metaTitle: Lagos Food Prices Today 2026: Rice, Garri, Beans & Eggs
metaDescription: Rice, garri, beans, yam and egg prices in Lagos today, with the 50kg bag price, best markets, and tips to stretch your naira. Updated 9 October 2026.
intro: If you are asking what food costs in Lagos today, the honest answer is: it depends on the market, the week, and whether you buy in bulk or by the kilo. Lagos is the most expensive city to rent and eat in, and also the place where money moves fastest. This page gives you the price bands we are tracking for 9 October 2026, with the sources and caveats clearly marked.

Treat the numbers as a planning guide. Prices in Lagos move with the harvest, transport cost and dollar pressure. We update this page from our daily price file, and every range is labelled indicative until a market check confirms it.

sections.h2: Rice, garri, beans, yam and eggs in Lagos today
paras: These are the five staples most Lagos households buy every week. The ranges below are indicative for 9 October 2026. They are planning numbers, not a receipt, and they should be checked against your own market visit before you commit a big budget.
Across the core five, the spread is wide. Rice is the biggest single cost, while eggs and garri are where small savings add up fastest over a month.
bullets: Rice (local/foreign, 1kg): ₦1,450 to ₦1,750 (per 1kg). 50kg bag long grain was about ₦60,000 in Lagos in mid-2026 per the state tracker.
Garri (white, 1kg): ₦850 to ₦1,100 (per 1kg). Garri is usually cheapest in the South-East, where it is processed.
Brown beans / oloyin (1kg): ₦2,200 to ₦2,800 (per 1kg). Beans prices rise in the lean season (roughly June to September).
Yam (white, 1kg): ₦1,800 to ₦2,400 (per 1kg). Sold by tuber. This is the per-kg equivalent for a medium tuber.
Eggs (1 piece, medium): ₦190 to ₦230 (per piece). A crate of 30 is usually cheaper per egg. Check for cracks before buying.

paras: A 50kg bag of rice in Lagos is around ₦60,000 in our indicative tracker. That works out to about ₦1,200 per kg before you add transport, storage and loss.
Buying a bag is only smart if you have dry storage and can use the rice within a few months. If you cannot, buy in smaller packs. Rice that gets damp goes sour and loses value quickly.
The national picture matters too. Lagos State's agriculture tracker reported a 50kg long-grain bag around ₦60,000 in mid-2026, and that is the benchmark most Lagos buyers are comparing against.
Markets are where Lagos prices are made. Here is where regulars go, and why.
bullets: Mile 12 International Market: rice, beans, garri, palm oil and wholesale food bags. Tip: Buy early (before 9am) for the best bags. Haggle on 50kg bags, not on single kilos.
Idumota Market: Lagos Island wholesale: provisions, dry goods and household staples. Tip: Go on weekdays. Weekends are crowded and prices bounce around more.
Oyingbo Market: fresh produce, fish, tomatoes and pepper that move fast. Tip: Fresh items are cheapest at the end of the day, but quality drops. Choose wisely.

sections.h2: How to stretch your naira in Lagos
paras: Lagos is the most expensive city to rent and eat in, and also the place where money moves fastest. That means the smartest buyers are the ones who plan their week, not the ones who react to every price change.
Start with a shopping list written from your real meals, not your wishes. Then decide which items to buy in bulk and which to buy in small amounts.
bullets: Buy staples in bulk once a month and fresh items weekly.
Compare at least two sellers before buying a big bag or a crate of eggs.
Set a weekly food cap and track it on your phone.
Cook in batches and freeze what you can, but check your power plan first.
Avoid buying on credit from the market unless you can repay on time.

sections.h2: Fuel, power and transport in Lagos
paras: Pump petrol in Lagos State was listed around ₦1,355 per litre in the latest NNPC retail list (9 October 2026).

Diesel is the key number for generator owners. The national median depot diesel price was ₦1,775 per litre on 6 October 2026, and Dangote's gantry diesel was ₦1,780 from 1 October. Pump and jerrycan diesel usually sits above depot prices, so budget for the gap.
Transport is often the biggest hidden cost in Lagos. Plan your trips, combine errands, and check the monthly transport budget in our cost-of-living calculator.

sections.h2: How Lagos compares with other cities
paras: Across our tracker, the cheapest city for rice is Kano and the most expensive is Abuja. Lagos ranks 8 out of 10 for rice.
For beans, Lagos ranks 8 out of 10. For eggs, it ranks 8. Use these rankings to decide whether to buy in Lagos or travel to a cheaper market.

sections.h2: What to do this week in Lagos
paras: Use this checklist before your next market run. It keeps your budget steady and stops the most common overspending.
bullets: Check the rice and beans range above and set a maximum you will pay.
Buy one staple in bulk and one in small packs so you can test prices.
Look at the cost-of-living calculator to see whether your monthly budget covers food and non-food costs.
Plan one cooking day for the week and buy only what that day needs.

faqs.q: Where is the cheapest garri in Lagos?
faqs.a: Garri is usually cheapest close to where it is processed. In Lagos, check the wholesale clusters first, then compare with the nearest retail market. Our indicative range is ₦850 to ₦1,100 per kg.

faqs.q: How much are eggs in Lagos today?
faqs.a: Our tracker shows about ₦190 to ₦230 per medium egg in Lagos. A crate of 30 is usually cheaper per egg, but check for cracks first.

faqs.a: Lagos sits at 8 out of 10 for rice in our tracker. Cost of living also depends on rent and transport, so compare the whole budget, not just the food.

paras: What each deduction means and how to check if your employer got it right.
bullets: Basic, housing and transport allowances make up gross pay. Check the breakdown.

NHF (National Housing Fund) is a deduction that can help you access a housing loan later.
